question.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Function Given in Implicit Form Using the Product Rule
question.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $7{x}^{3}{y}^{3}$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}7{x}^{3}{y}^{3}+3{y}^{2} & =12{x}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{3}{y}^{3}+3{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{3}{y}^{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{2}) \\ [21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+21{x}^{2}{y}^{3}]+6y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =24x \\ 21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+21{x}^{2}{y}^{3}+6y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =24x\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =24x-21{x}^{2}{y}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+6y) & =24x-21{x}^{2}{y}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{8x-7{x}^{2}{y}^{3}}{7{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+2y}\end{aligned}
$$
